key_insight: This paper maps out important training choices in continuous diffusion language models, showing that small design levers like self-conditioning and embedding choices can significantly affect performance. The main takeaway is that CDLMs are becoming competitive, but their behavior depends strongly on how they are trained.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of clear guidance on which training and architecture choices matter most for continuous diffusion language models, especially compared with better-understood continuous domains like images and video.
method: Systematically studies key design levers in CDLMs, with a focus on self-conditioning and embedding-related choices.
Compares training configurations to identify which settings improve language generation quality and efficiency.
Analyzes how these levers influence model behavior to provide practical design guidance for future CDLMs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work offers a clearer roadmap for building stronger continuous diffusion language models. It helps reduce trial-and-error by highlighting which training decisions are most likely to improve sample quality, controllability, and efficiency.
visual_elements: A design-space map showing the main CDLM training levers and their effects
A side-by-side comparison chart of performance with and without self-conditioning
A pipeline diagram of a continuous diffusion language model for text generation
Icons representing speed, control, and quality to summarize practical benefits
paper_title: On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Oscar Davis, Daan Roos, Alice Bizeul, Amitis Shidani, Victor Turrisi
